The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to test a causal model with hidden variables, it is not sufficient to test the conditional independencies implied by the d-separation.
, in the presence of hidden variables, causal models can have testable implications that go beyond the standard conditional independence constraints.
, in the presence of hidden variables, the causal structure of the data-generating process is often testable, even when the functional constraints are non-linear.
